question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is related with promotion of co - operative societies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 43 B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Article 43 B was inserted into the Constitution of India by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.

• This article is specifically aimed at promoting voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of co-operative societies.

• Co-operative societies are institutions that are voluntarily formed by individuals with common economic, social, and cultural needs and interests.

• Promotion of co-operative societies aims to enhance economic and social development, particularly in rural areas, by encouraging self-help and mutual aid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Article 31 B**

• Article 31 B of the Indian Constitution was introduced by the First Amendment in 1951.

• It provides protection to laws included in the Ninth Schedule from being challenged and invalidated on the ground of violation of fundamental rights.

• The Ninth Schedule was created to give effect to certain land reform measures and prevent them from being challenged in courts.

• **Article 51 A**

• Article 51 A specifies the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India.

• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

• It includes duties such as respecting the national symbols, protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.

• **Article 39 A**

• Article 39 A directs the State to provide free legal aid to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.

• This article emphasizes the importance of equal justice and free legal aid.

• It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
